section.name: Functions Reference
section.p: This page documents the native utility functions added by BreakTest. For inherited functions, use the Apache JMeter reference linked below.
For the generic JMeter-compatible behavior behind this topic, use the official Apache JMeter documentation.

subsection.name: Native BreakTest utility functions
subsection.p: These functions ship with BreakTest; no Custom JMeter Functions plugin is required. Function names are case-sensitive. Arguments can contain variables or nested functions and are evaluated on each call. Escape literal commas as \,. Do not surround string arguments with quotes. Where supported, the final result-variable argument stores the returned value; omitting it or leaving it empty only returns the value. For functions requiring a final result-variable position, keep the trailing comma even when no result variable is needed. To pass empty text to a one-text-argument function, use a variable with an empty value or an empty result-variable position, for example ${__SHA256(,)}. Invalid arguments fail function evaluation. All byte-to-text decoders use UTF-8, replacing malformed UTF-8 sequences with the replacement character.

subsection.name: __chooseRandom
subsection.p: Chooses one of the values before the final, required result-variable argument. Use an empty final argument to discard the variable. Only the selected value is evaluated.

subsection.name: __doubleSum
subsection.p: Adds two or more Java floating-point numbers. The final argument is always the result-variable name (which may be empty); it is never added.

subsection.name: __env
subsection.p: Reads an environment variable on the machine running the test. Arguments: environment name, optional result-variable name, optional default. If unset and no default is supplied, returns the environment name.

subsection.name: __isDefined
subsection.p: Returns 1 when the named thread variable exists, otherwise 0. An empty value is defined. Pass its name, not its expanded value.

subsection.name: __MD5
subsection.p: MD5 digest of UTF-8 text, returned as lowercase hexadecimal. An optional second argument stores the result in a thread variable.

subsection.name: __SHA256
subsection.p: SHA-256 digest of UTF-8 text, returned as lowercase hexadecimal. An optional second argument stores the result in a thread variable.

subsection.name: __base64Encode
subsection.p: Encodes UTF-8 text as standard Base64 with padding. An optional second argument stores the result in a thread variable.

subsection.name: __base64Decode
subsection.p: Decodes standard Base64 into UTF-8 text. Invalid Base64 is rejected. An optional second argument stores the result in a thread variable.

subsection.name: __base64UrlEncode
subsection.p: Encodes UTF-8 text as URL-safe Base64 without padding. An optional second argument stores the result in a thread variable.

subsection.name: __base64UrlDecode
subsection.p: Decodes URL-safe Base64 into UTF-8 text, with or without padding. Invalid Base64 is rejected. An optional second argument stores the result in a thread variable.

subsection.name: __strLen
subsection.p: Returns the Java string length (UTF-16 code units). An optional second argument stores the result in a thread variable.

subsection.name: __uppercase
subsection.p: Converts text to uppercase using locale-independent rules. An optional second argument stores the result in a thread variable.

subsection.name: __lowercase
subsection.p: Converts text to lowercase using locale-independent rules. An optional second argument stores the result in a thread variable.

subsection.name: __stringToHex
subsection.p: Encodes UTF-8 bytes as lowercase hexadecimal without a prefix or separators. An optional second argument stores the result in a thread variable.

subsection.name: __hexToString
subsection.p: Decodes hexadecimal bytes into UTF-8 text. Accepts either letter case; rejects non-hex characters and odd lengths. An optional second argument stores the result in a thread variable.

subsection.name: __trim
subsection.p: Removes leading and trailing Java Unicode whitespace. An optional second argument stores the result in a thread variable.

subsection.name: __substring
subsection.p: Arguments: text, zero-based inclusive begin index, exclusive end index, optional result variable. Indices use UTF-16 code units; invalid ranges are rejected.

subsection.name: __strReplace
subsection.p: Arguments: text, literal search text, literal replacement, optional result variable. Replaces every occurrence.

subsection.name: __strReplaceRegex
subsection.p: Arguments: text, Java regular expression, replacement, optional result variable. Replaces all matches. Replacement supports Java group references such as $1; escape backslashes and commas for the function parser.

subsection.name: __iterationNum
subsection.p: Returns the current thread-group iteration, starting at 1 during a run. Returns 0 before iteration begins or when no thread variables exist. Takes no arguments.

subsection.name: __if
subsection.p: Arguments: actual text, expected text, value when equal, value when unequal, optional result variable. Comparison is exact and case-sensitive; only the selected branch is evaluated.

subsection.name: __epochMilliSeconds
subsection.p: Returns the current Unix epoch timestamp in milliseconds, independent of the local timezone. Equivalent to ${__time()}. Optional argument: result variable. Evaluated on each call.
${__epochMilliSeconds()} or ${__epochMilliSeconds(timestamp)}

subsection.name: __epochSeconds
subsection.p: Returns the current Unix epoch timestamp in whole seconds, independent of the local timezone. Optional argument: result variable. Evaluated on each call; the inherited ${__time(/1000)} also returns epoch seconds.

subsection.name: __caseFormat
subsection.p: Arguments: text, optional case mode (default LOWER_CAMEL_CASE), optional result variable. Splits spaces, hyphens, underscores and camel-case boundaries. Modes (case-insensitive): LOWER_CAMEL_CASE, UPPER_CAMEL_CASE, SNAKE_CASE/LOWER_UNDERSCORE, KEBAB_CASE/LISP_CASE/SPINAL_CASE/LOWER_HYPHEN, TRAIN_CASE (uppercase with hyphens), UPPER_UNDERSCORE. An unknown mode returns the original text.

section.p: Compatibility names such as jmeter.properties, JMeterThread, ApacheJMeter.jar, and org.apache.jmeter may still appear in BreakTest where they are part of the file format, runtime API, or plugin contract.
